title: Remove an avocado stone
instruction: Remove the stone from the avocado half without crushing the flesh, and put the stone in the waste dish.
setup: One firm-ripe Hass avocado half, about 100 x 65 x 35 mm, cut-side up with its 35–40 mm stone still attached; a 300 x 240 x 18 mm wooden chopping board; and a 110 mm diameter, 24 mm deep waste dish. The fruit is centred on the board, with its narrow end toward the left arm. The dish is 180 mm toward the right arm. Both hands start open. Use clean removable food-safe pad covers.
scoring: 1.0 if the stone is fully removed and rests in the waste dish, the avocado remains intact on the board, and both hands have released for three seconds. 0.5 if the intact stone is fully clear of the fruit but not yet released in the dish. Otherwise 0. A torn skin or crushed/torn flesh patch larger than 1 cm² scores 0. Use the final video and a ruler beside the fruit.
fidelity: Native colliding fruit, stone, dish and robot fingers. Passive bonds resist stone extraction and allow the flesh to break under excessive load; no object is attached to a hand. The fruit is a coarse assembly rather than a deformable tissue model. Its 7 N extraction and 12 N flesh-bond thresholds are engineering estimates, not measurements. Native demo reaches full score with contact grasps.
context: Removing a stubborn avocado stone calls for a firm grip on the stone while protecting the soft flesh.
reset_notes: Use a fresh firm-ripe Hass half at 18–22 °C, cut immediately before a trial. Reject visibly overripe, split or already loose-stoned halves. Use a single grocery batch and record size/ripeness. Clean the board, dish and removable covers between trials.
